requirements.quote: The version of QUIC defined in this document is identified as 0x00000001
requirements.condition: When identifying the QUIC version defined by this specification
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify this version with a different value.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encoded or recognized version identifier can be compared with the fixed 32-bit value.

requirements.quote: The version of QUIC defined in this document is identified as 0x00000001 and uses TLS as described in [QUIC-TLS]
requirements.required_behavior: Use TLS as the cryptographic handshake protocol.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different cryptographic handshake protocol for this version.
requirements.why_checkable: The handshake protocol selected for version 0x00000001 can be observed in implementation code and runtime negotiation.

requirements.quote: QUIC uses the CRYPTO frame (Section 19.6) to transmit the cryptographic handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit the data using CRYPTO frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transmit cryptographic handshake data as ordinary application data.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame construction and parsing can be inspected to determine whether handshake bytes are carried in CRYPTO frames.

requirements.quote: QUIC provides reliable, ordered delivery of the cryptographic handshake data.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide reliable delivery and deliver the data in order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not expose missing, duplicated, or out-of-order handshake data to the cryptographic handshake consumer.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss, duplication, and reordering tests can verify the byte stream delivered to the handshake layer.

requirements.quote: QUIC packet protection is used to encrypt as much of the handshake protocol as possible.
requirements.required_behavior: Encrypt as much of the handshake protocol as possible using QUIC packet protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase "as much ... as possible" does not define a self-contained boundary for which handshake material must be encrypted.

requirements.quote:
The cryptographic handshake MUST provide the following properties:

   *  authenticated key exchange
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not establish connection keys through an unauthenticated key exchange.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake authentication and key-establishment behavior can be tested with valid and unauthenticated peers.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not complete a handshake in which the server is unauthenticated.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can attempt handshake completion without valid server authentication and verify rejection.

requirements.required_behavior: Support operation in which the client is authenticated and operation in which it is not authenticated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make client authentication an unconditional property of every connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake tests can verify both authenticated-client and unauthenticated-client configurations.

requirements.quote: every connection produces distinct and unrelated keys
requirements.required_behavior: Produce keys that are distinct from and unrelated to the keys of every other connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse connection keys or derive keys with a relation that compromises independence between connections.
requirements.why_checkable: Repeated connection establishment can be instrumented to compare resulting key material and its derivation inputs.

requirements.quote: keying material is usable for packet protection for both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: When the applicable 0-RTT or 1-RTT encryption level is available
requirements.required_behavior: Provide keying material usable for packet protection of both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not establish a handshake whose keying material cannot protect either required packet class.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime tests can verify that derived keying material successfully protects and unprotects both packet classes.

requirements.quote: authenticated exchange of values for transport parameters of both endpoints
requirements.condition: When exchanging endpoint transport parameters during the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: Authenticate the transport-parameter values of both endpoints.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept unauthenticated transport-parameter values from either endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: Tampering tests can determine whether modification of either endpoint's transport parameters is detected.

requirements.quote: confidentiality protection for server transport parameters
requirements.required_behavior: Provide confidentiality protection for the server transport parameters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not expose server transport parameters without the required confidentiality protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet inspection can determine whether server transport parameters are exposed outside protected handshake content.

requirements.quote: authenticated negotiation of an application protocol
requirements.condition: When negotiating the application protocol during the cryptographic handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not complete the negotiation based on unauthenticated application-protocol selection data.
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiation tampering tests can verify that unauthenticated modification or selection is rejected.

requirements.quote: The CRYPTO frame can be sent in different packet number spaces (Section 12.3).
requirements.why_checkable: The passage says that different packet number spaces can carry CRYPTO frames but does not identify within this chunk exactly which spaces or packet types permit them.

requirements.quote: The offsets used by CRYPTO frames to ensure ordered delivery of cryptographic handshake data start from zero in each packet number space.
requirements.condition: For CRYPTO-frame offset accounting in each packet number space
requirements.required_behavior: Start the cryptographic handshake data offset at zero independently in each packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue a CRYPTO offset sequence from one packet number space into another or initialize it to a nonzero value.
requirements.why_checkable: The first CRYPTO stream offset and offset tracking state can be inspected independently for every packet number space.

requirements.quote: Once the handshake is complete, endpoints are able to exchange application data freely.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit endpoints to exchange application data.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can complete the handshake and verify bidirectional application-data exchange.

requirements.quote: An endpoint validates support for ECN by observing whether the ACK frames acknowledging the first packets it sends carry ECN counts
requirements.condition: When an endpoint validates ECN support using packets sent during the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: Observe whether ACK frames acknowledging the endpoint's first sent packets carry ECN counts.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the described validation as satisfied without examining ECN counts in those ACK frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Focused tests can control ACK contents for the first sent packets and inspect the endpoint's ECN validation state.

requirements.quote: Endpoints MUST explicitly negotiate an application protocol.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer or silently assume the application protocol without explicit negotiation.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake traces and connection state can show whether an explicit application-protocol negotiation occurred before establishment.

requirements.quote: Endpoints MUST explicitly negotiate an application protocol.  This avoids situations where there is a disagreement about the protocol that is in use.
requirements.condition: When the endpoints' application-protocol negotiation does not yield agreement
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not proceed with endpoints using different understandings of the application protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The normative negotiation requirement and its adjacent stated purpose directly imply that connection establishment must not leave the endpoints with disagreeing application protocols.
